ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of foreign and domestic PEPs, family members and close associates under the AML/CFT Act of 12 November 2004 and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2022, consistent with FATF Recommendations 12 and 25; automated real-time sanctions screening against the UN Security Council consolidated list, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (FSP), OFAC SDN list, UK HMT list and Luxembourg Ministry of Finance asset-freeze measures under the Law of 19 December 2020; enhanced due diligence for PEPs, high-risk third-country UBOs and complex ownership chains; adverse media and negative news screening; ongoing transaction monitoring and event-driven re-screening throughout the corporate lifecycle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessible via e-Justice portal (www.lbr.lu / www.guichet.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory documents and the company name must be submitted in French, German, Luxembourgish or English in the Roman/Latin alphabet; non-Latin script names are not accepted by the RCS until transliterated into Latin characters; the legal form suffix 'société à responsabilité limitée' or 'S.à r.l.' is mandatory for SARL companies; the chosen name must be distinguishable from all existing RCS-registered names, must not be identical or confusingly similar, and must not contravene public order, good morals or mandatory legal form indications.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANQUE - BANK (regulated, prior CSSF authorization required)
ASSURANCE - INSURANCE (regulated, prior CAA authorization required)
S.A. or other legal-form tokens inconsistent with the actual SARL structure
Words implying public appeal for savings (appel public à l'épargne)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The Luxembourg RCS does not issue a separate name-reservation certificate; the name is blocked from the date the notarial deed of incorporation is signed before the Luxembourg notary and must be filed for registration within one month. Upon rejection, the notary or corporate counsel shall obtain the RCS registrar's written refusal stating grounds; deficiencies may be cured by re-filing through the e-Justice portal. If the refusal persists, the applicant may file a petition before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Chambre commerciale) against the registrar's decision within 15 days of notification, following Art. 44 of the RCS procedure and the general rules of the Law of 10 August 1915. In parallel, the notary may reserve an alternative cleared name and execute an amending deed (acte rectificatif). Extension of the 30-day window is not available as a formal mechanism; therefore the applicant must monitor RCS clearance immediately prior to deed execution.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office for this industry. Luxembourg law (Art. 77-79 of the Law of 10 August 1915) requires a real registered office (siège social) within the Grand Duchy. For a licensed IVD manufacturer and medical device establishment under EU Regulation 2017/746 (IVDR), the registered office and operational manufacturing site must be a genuine physical location; a mail-drop or virtual-office address is insufficient and will fail the substance checks applied by the RBE, the tax authorities and the licensing authorities. A licensed domiciliation agent may be used only for the administrative seat if the actual production and management substance is at a separate Luxembourg address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 60% annual probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection: mandatory supervisory inspections by the Luxembourg Ministry of Health (Direction de la Santé) and the Laboratoire National de Santé for IVDR compliance, plus workplace safety inspections by the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) and substance verification visits by the RBE/CSSF in the context of AML/CFT continuing due diligence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), together with the Law of 23 September 2020 modernising company law; SARL governed by Articles 710-1 to 710-25; supplemented by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 December 2008 on the Trade and Companies Register (RCS/RESA) and Regulation (EU) 2017/746 for the IVD manufacturing scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Luxembourg; applications are filed electronically via the MyGuichet.lu portal and the eJustices platform, with the notary acting as the statutory intermediary.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif / statuts) certified by a Luxembourg notary, followed by mandatory publication of the incorporation particulars in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) and registration on the official RCS application form (formulaire C); the RCS extract (extrait) constitutes the certificate of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL minimum share capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation; cash contributions must be paid into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) opened with a Luxembourg credit institution or with the Caisse de Consignation; the banker's blockage attestation must be remitted to the notary, and the funds are released only upon effective registration in the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned founding shareholder of [Company Name] SARL (the 'Company'), acting in the capacity of the corporate governance body, hereby approves the following first resolutions. 1. The Articles of Association dated [date] are adopted, and the share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 12,000 shares of EUR 1.00 each, is subscribed in full, to be paid up against the blocked escrow attestation delivered by [Bank]. 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg. 3. [Name] is appointed gérant (manager) of the Company, with sole signature authority and full powers to open bank accounts, sign the RCS, tax, and licensing filings, and represent the Company. 4. All pre-registration acts done by the gérant are ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Clearance and Availability Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online search portal and MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an exhaustive search in the RCS database for identical or confusingly similar names; verify the absence of conflicting trademark registrations at the Luxembourg Intellectual Property Office (IPIL); confirm that the chosen name contains the statutory suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or 'SARL'; file the name-clearance request electronically and obtain a preliminary written clearance note before drafting the articles of association.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name variants (primary and two fallbacks)
Founder identification details (full name, address, date and place of birth)
Description of the corporate object (manufacture of microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers)
Signed mandate of the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for similarity or public-order concerns, immediately file a revised proposal with a new distinctive element; fallback names pre-cleared in the same application avoid any delay to the notarial timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Share-Capital Escrow Account and Deposit of Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (deposit bank) or the Caisse de Consignation (Luxembourg Consignment Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) in the name of 'Company SARL en formation'; effect the cash deposit aggregating at least EUR 12,000 by wire transfer from the founders' own accounts; instruct the bank to issue an irrevocable blockage attestation (attestation de blocage) in favour of the notary, stating that the funds are blocked until the company's RCS registration is produced; deliver this attestation to the notary for incorporation.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC/AML forms and identity documents of founders and ultimate beneficial owners
Source-of-funds declaration and economic purpose statement for the IVD manufacturing activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If enhanced due-diligence queries arise, provide certified UBO documentation, bank references and source-of-wealth evidence; the blockage attestation can be reissued by the bank without cost once the queries are cured, and the delay is absorbed before the notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Deed of Incorporation and RESA Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary appointed within the Ordre des Notaires du Luxembourg; RESA publication service of the Ministry of Justice operated through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Remit the blockage attestation, draft articles, identity and UBO documents, and the manager's written consent to the notary; the notary verifies the lawful object, the fully paid-up capital, the registered office, and the manager's legal capacity; after signature of the notarial deed of incorporation, the notary triggers the online RESA publication of the statutory particulars and assembles the RCS registration package.
required_dossiers: Banker's blockage attestation evidencing EUR 12,000 minimum capital
Certified passports or identity cards of founding shareholders and the appointed gérant
Draft articles of association covering manufacturing of microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers
Written acceptance of office by the appointed gérant
UBO declaration form and source-of-funds evidence
Proof of availability of the registered office (lease title or occupancy permission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a legal defect such as an object clause misaligned with the IVD scope or insufficient capital evidence, execute a corrective notarial addendum (acte rectificatif) before filing; a same-week correction does not restart the RESA publication timeline.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxation: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), 45-47 avenue de la Gare, L-1611 Luxembourg, portal https://impotsdirects.public.lu. Indirect taxation (VAT, registration duties, excise): Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), 1-3 avenue Guillaume, L-1651 Luxembourg, portal https://aedt.public.lu. Unified e-government filing platform: MyGuichet.lu (https://myguichet.lu). Customs administration: Administration des douanes et accises operating under EU Union Customs Code. Health-sector licensing for IVD manufacturing: Luxembourg Ministry of Health (Direction de la Santé) and EU Regulation (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: SOP: (1) Execute a notarial deed of incorporation and register the SARL with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); the State IT Centre (CTIE) automatically assigns the corporate national identification number (matricule), which serves as the direct-tax TIN. (2) Obtain the business licence (autorisation d'établissement) from the Ministry of the Economy for manufacturing activities; IVD producers additionally require regulatory licensing under the EU IVDR and Ministry of Health notification. (3) File electronic VAT registration with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu using the form Déclaration d'inscription à la TVA before commencing taxable supplies; the AEDT issues a VAT identification number in the format LU plus 8 digits and a VAT certificate. (4) Notify the competent ACD local tax office of the registered seat to open the corporate income tax file; annual CIT and municipal business tax filing is mandatory regardless of profitability. (5) Non-established foreign suppliers or zero-turnover structures may be required to appoint a Luxembourg VAT and customs representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the Luxembourg SARL is a resident full taxpayer at entity level: subject to corporate income tax at 17%, municipal business tax at the communal rate (6.75% in Luxembourg City), solidarity surcharge at 7% of corporate income tax, and net wealth tax at 0.5% with applicable allowances. The territorial scope reaches worldwide income, relieved by Luxembourg's treaty network and the domestic participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains. No pass-through or disregarded-entity status exists under Luxembourg domestic law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg domestic law provides no check-the-box or pass-through election; the SARL is mandatorily an entity-level CIT taxpayer. Available elections: (i) full fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under LIR Article 164bis for Luxembourg-resident groups holding at least 95% of eligible subsidiaries; (ii) the Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on qualifying new equity; (iii) the 80% IP-box income exemption under LIR Article 50bis on net qualifying IP income, subject to OECD nexus substantiation. For US federal tax purposes, the SARL is not a per se corporation, so a Form 8832 check-the-box election may classify it as a partnership or disregarded entity; hybrid mismatch consequences are neutralized or reported under Luxembourg ATAD transposition (LIR Articles 168ter/168quater) and DAC6 disclosure rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA), governed by the Loi TVA of 12 February 1979 as amended, aligned with EU Directive 2006/112/EC; registration, filing, and assessment are administered by the AEDT through the MyGuichet.lu platform.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover is the domestic small-business exemption ceiling for Luxembourg-established businesses; exceeding this threshold triggers mandatory VAT registration. In practice a manufacturing SARL supplying IVD equipment to B2B customers, importing raw materials, or making intra-EU acquisitions is required to register irrespective of the threshold. Non-established foreign suppliers have no threshold: registration is due before the first taxable supply in Luxembourg. Intra-EU distance sales of goods exceed the EUR 10,000 pan-EU annual threshold and become taxable in the destination member state.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no real-time fiscal clearance regime, no digital stamping mandate, and no API-based continuous transaction controls for domestic VAT invoices. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only to business-to-government (B2G) invoicing via the national Peppol-compliant platform, phased in for central government transactions from 1 January 2024 and for broader public entities thereafter. Invoice content, sequential numbering, and 30-day issuance requirements follow Loi TVA Articles 57-58. VAT periodical returns (monthly for large taxpayers, quarterly for the small-business regime) and EC Sales Lists must be filed electronically through the AEDT e-filing portal. Luxembourg is transposing the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) reform, which will introduce mandatory e-invoicing and near-real-time digital reporting for cross-border B2B supplies by 1 July 2030.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero per cent VAT applies to (i) final exports of goods outside the European Union under Loi TVA Article 44(1)(1), provided the goods leave EU territory within 90 days of dispatch and the exporter retains complete transport and customs evidence; and (ii) intra-EU dispatches of IVD equipment to a customer holding a valid EU VAT identification number under Article 44(1)(2), supported by compliant invoicing and EC Sales List filing. Supplies of microfluidic cartridges, immunoassay analyzers, and directly related calibration or installation services are zero-rated where the goods physically exit the EU or the service is received by a non-EU recipient. Export refunds are claimed through periodic VAT returns; excess credit positions are repayable by the AEDT within statutory timeframes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration (SAD with Movement Reference Number (MRN)) lodged with Luxembourg Customs and Excise
Commercial invoice (final) denominated in the contract currency, describing the goods, Incoterms, and the export supply
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or CMR consignment note evidencing physical movement from Luxembourg or the EU
Customs exit confirmation generated by the EU electronic export system (departure message or export proof within the 90-day departure window)
EC Sales List (recapitulative statement) and customer order referencing the recipient's valid EU VAT identification number for intra-EU zero-rated supplies
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103/MT202 credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds within the 180-day repatriation benchmark
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may claw back incorrectly zero-rated VAT within the standard five-year limitation period, extended to ten years for fraud or intentional concealment, reassessing the VAT at 17% plus default interest of 0.8% per month under Article 39 Loi TVA. Administrative fines under Articles 62 and 63 Loi TVA range from EUR 250 to EUR 250,000 and may reach four times the evaded tax for fraudulent conduct. Criminal tax fraud (fraude fiscale) is punishable under the General Tax Law and the Criminal Code by imprisonment of one to five years and fines from EUR 12,500 to EUR 125,000. Customs offences attract penalties under the Union Customs Code (Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, Article 42) and Luxembourg customs law, including confiscation and per-declaration fines. The AEDT, ACD, and customs administration cross-verify export declarations, VIES counterparty status, and banking receipts, triggering joint audits and mutual assistance procedures. Luxembourg imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is applied as a prudential substantiation and transfer-pricing convention, and failure to repatriate within that period may raise commercial substance and pricing audit questions rather than a standalone VAT penalty.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), a Eurosystem member, exercises national central-bank functions for TARGET2/T2 settlement, liquidity management, and statistical balance-of-payments reporting; the European Central Bank (ECB) sets euro-area monetary policy and administers foreign-exchange reserves. The Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the competent authority for bank licensing, ongoing prudential supervision, AML/CFT enforcement, and payment-services/EMI regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Luxembourg applies the EU capital-movement freedoms (Art. 63 TFEU) and Directive 88/361/EEC Annex I; there are no exchange-control permits, investment approvals, or profit-repatriation licences for a Luxembourg SARL. Remittance of dividends or liquidation proceeds is subject only to corporate-law gates: annual net-asset test (net assets must exceed subscribed capital plus non-distributable reserves, including the 5% legal reserve), notarial/board formalities, statutory auditor confirmation, and a 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (treaty-reduced if applicable). No central-bank or CSSF consent is required for shareholder distributions or capital reduction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable in Luxembourg and the euro area. IVD export proceeds may be retained in EUR or any foreign currency, freely deployed, converted, or reinvested without mandatory surrender, conversion ratios, or holding-period constraints. Enterprises are only obliged to file periodic balance-of-payments statistical declarations with the BCL (e.g., forms for trade in goods/services), which have no effect on the disponibility of funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + Operational Account with dedicated documentary-credit and trade-services desk
Capital Escrow Account + Operational Account + FX/Treasury hedging line
Capital Escrow Account + Operational Account with trade-finance and supply-chain solutions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited. EU-authorised EMIs/payment institutions (e.g., Airwallex, Wise Business, Revolut Business) passporting into Luxembourg under PSD2 may lawfully execute low-value operational wire transfers, supplier disbursements, and FX conversions, and provide virtual IBANs. However, they cannot issue the statutory blocked-capital certificate that a notary requires for SARL incorporation, and they do not operate UCP 600 documentary-credit desks, LC advising/confirming, or trade-finance lending. Feasibility Rating: Medium only as a supplementary disbursement rail; not viable as the primary relationship bank for SWIFT LC/MT103 trade flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg credit institutions require a physical KYC/identity verification for managing directors and ultimate beneficial owners of an enhanced-due-diligence manufacturing SARL. At least one authorised director with individual signature rights must attend an initial in-person meeting at the bank's Luxembourg branch or appear before a Luxembourg notary with a notarised corporate mandate. Non-EU resident directors/UBOs can usually complete verification through an apostilled and notarised power of attorney, a physical appointment at an upstream correspondent bank, or at a Luxembourg honorary consulate; fully remote/video-only onboarding is not accepted for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced entity engaged in documentary trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity: complex multi-layer ownership, nominee arrangements, or a non-EU shareholder chain where individuals owning >25% cannot be clearly identified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract from the Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); full organisational chart and capitalisation table; constitutional documents, register extracts, and audited financial statements of each intermediate entity; passport copies and proof-of-address for each natural-person UBO; sworn declaration confirming no undisclosed nominees or indirect control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or high-risk source of initial share capital and subsequent working-capital funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12 months of bank statements and wealth records of each contributing shareholder; salary slips and confirmed tax returns; notarised deed of incorporation; sale-and-purchase agreements if funding derives from a prior business disposal; sworn statement as to the absence of third-party temporary deposits; audited financials of any funding corporate shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flags: over/under-invoicing, shipment to embargoed or sanctions-exposed countries, or unexpected intermediary chains in IVD/medical exports.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transactional file for the first ten counterparties: master distribution agreements, pro-forma invoices, final commercial invoices, Incoterms 2020 terms, Luxembourg export declarations (single-window/electronic customs), bills of lading or airway bills, insurance certificates, end-user certificates, CE-marking/IVDR documentation under Regulation (EU) 2017/746, ISO 13485 certificate, and EU/OFAC/UN denied-party screening reports for all trade parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Liquidity and round-tripping suspicion: high-velocity inbound and outbound flows disproportionate to the stated working-capital cycle, or multiple rapid FX conversions without commercial rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved 12-month cash-flow forecast; detailed cost-of-goods-sold build-up (raw materials, labour, logistics, manufacturing overhead); supplier purchase orders and customer sales contracts; inventory movement ledger; tax-compliant commercial invoices; and a treasury policy memo explaining collection/payment terms (e.g., 30–60 days LC terms against 0–15 day pre-financing).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status or adverse media concerning the healthcare/IVD sector, including COVID-19 test fraud or health-corruption allegations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full CV and professional references; EUDAMED/IVDR registration and notified-body certificates; product certifications (CE, optional FDA 510(k)); an externally prepared source-of-wealth report; documentation of institutional customers (public health tenders, hospital group contracts); appointment of an independent compliance officer; and the LU-SARL's written AML/CFT risk policy.
